key_insight: BAGEL exposes a large gap between general LLM performance and specialized animal-related expertise by providing a unified closed-book benchmark drawn from scientific and reference sources. It shows that state-of-the-art models often mispredict or are poorly calibrated on taxonomy, behavior, ecology and bioacoustic queries.
problem_solved: There was no standardized, closed-book benchmark to measure how well language models know specialized animal facts and concepts; BAGEL fills this gap by assembling diverse, high-quality animal knowledge sources and a unified evaluation protocol.
method: Curate questions and ground-truth facts from diverse scientific and reference sources (e.g., bioRxiv, Global Biotic Interactions, Xeno-canto, Wikipedia).
Design closed-book, prompt-based tasks covering taxonomy, behavior, ecology, species interactions, and bioacoustics with controlled answer formats.
Evaluate multiple LLMs using accuracy, calibration and error-type analyses to quantify gaps and failure modes.
impact: BAGEL gives ML practitioners a targeted tool to identify and fix animal-knowledge weaknesses in LLMs—informing data collection, fine-tuning, and model auditing for ecology, conservation, and biology applications.
visual_elements: Source-map collage: icons/logos for bioRxiv, Global Biotic Interactions, Xeno-canto, Wikipedia with a flow into a dataset box.
Task composition chart: pie or stacked bar showing breakdown (taxonomy, behavior, ecology, interactions, bioacoustics).
Model performance heatmap: rows = models, columns = task types, color = accuracy/calibration to highlight gaps.
Error vignette panel: 2–3 example Q→model answer→ground-truth with annotated failure modes (hallucination, misclassification, uncertainty).
paper_title: BAGEL: Benchmarking Animal Knowledge Expertise in Language Models
paper_authors: Jiacheng Shen, Masato Hagiwara, Milad Alizadeh, Ellen Gilsenan-McMahon, Marius Miron
